subject: general
question: What does the word "proletarian" most nearly mean as used in the passage?

options.text: Involving working-class life and social issues

solution: The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. involving working-class life and social issues. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The word **"proletarian"** means: • Relating to the proletariat, the working-class people, especially the industrial working class. (कामकाजी वर्ग के जीवन और सामाजिक मुद्दों से संबंधित) • The correct meaning of "proletarian" in the given context is **"involving working-class life and social issues."** • **Example from the passage:** The novel depicts the harsh realities of proletarian life in the city. • **Example:** His poetry often highlighted the struggles and triumphs of proletarian communities. Therefore, the word “proletarian” most nearly means: **involving working-class life and social issues.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences: • **Related to science and technology** (विज्ञान और प्रौद्योगिकी से संबंधित): Modern advancements and innovations in various scientific fields. • **Example:** The conference covered topics related to science and technology, focusing on recent breakthroughs. • **Focused on romantic relationships** (रोमांटिक संबंधों पर केंद्रित): Concentrated on love and personal emotional connections. • **Example:** The film's plot was focused on romantic relationships between the main characters. • **Concentrating on futuristic imagination** (भविष्य की कल्पना पर केंद्रित): Idealistic planning or speculation about future possibilities and inventions. • **Example:** The novel was concentrating on futuristic imagination, depicting a world transformed by technology. 1c8:Te45, The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. imaginary or theoretical, not yet proven.
